title: fix: accept Gemini TTS usage that lists the voice's audio prompt
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16435

- Google's speech usage now has an `audio` input entry for the voice's built-in prompt (~201 tokens), next to the `text` entry
- The parser accepted only `text`, so it rejected every Google reply. Since 2026-10-04 every Google call failed with "invalid usage" (73 on 10-06)
- Each rejected call fell back to OpenRouter. Google had already generated (and billed) the audio, so we paid twice, and the fallback 502s when OpenRouter's usage record takes over 60 s (about 2 in 3 today)
- Now accepts the `audio` entry and bills text input only, which matches Google's price list and OpenRouter's record for the same call

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Google reply with an `audio` entry | rejected → OpenRouter | accepted |
| Billed input tokens | — | text only (e.g. 5, not 206) |

Checked: gen tsc, 22 Gemini TTS tests (new one uses the shape Google returns today), Biome. A real Google reply from today fails main's parser with the same "invalid usage" error as production and parses with this fix (6 text, 56 audio tokens). The reply still includes the zero-valued cached/thought/tool counters.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: Gemini finds its voice again
gist.blurb: Gemini TTS replies include a little audio prompt for the built-in voice. The parser makes room for it, so the speech can come through without taking a detour.
gist.summary: Gemini TTS accepts Google's usage records with an audio entry for the built-in voice prompt while counting only text input tokens for billing, matching Google's price list.
gist.impact: Google-generated speech is accepted directly instead of falling back to OpenRouter, and a request with 5 text tokens and about 201 voice-prompt audio tokens counts 5 billed input tokens rather than 206.
